newsitem.title: USA: Emery Worldwide sees decline in belly space.
newsitem.headline: Emery Worldwide sees decline in belly space.

text.p: Cargo space on passenger airlines will continue to decline, a top official of Emery Worldwide Airlines predicted here this week.

As airlines focus on the passenger's need for frequent flights and switch to smaller aircraft, belly capacity will continue to decline, said Willard H. Scherrer, senior vice president, Emery Worldwide Airlines, the airline of Emery Worldwide, a division of Consolidated Freightways Inc.
Speaking to the Cargo Facts Used Aircraft Symposium, Scherrer also said Emery was looking to acquire widebody aircraft.
"The business already exceeds capacity on many routes, so we are looking to widebody aircraft," he said.

Emery currently flies 36 Douglas DC-8s, 17 Boeing 727 and three DC-9s. It also uses 20 Boeing 727s for its contract with the United States Postal Service. Like most cargo companies, Emery buys used aircraft "because our level of utilization is low," Scherrer said.
About two-thirds of freighter aircraft are used, a Cargo Facts study found.
